conclusions.result: One intentMacCacheKey helper now supplies identical suffixed key for lookup/population and workspace retirement. retireWorkspace removes the actual private HMAC entry; it does not clear another workspace or delete durable IndexedDB material. This closes the specific retained-reference defect.

Test uses indexedDB:null from existing deps, so no durable key reload can hide the cache behavior. Both pre/post intents use the same canonical operation/target/body/clientIntent and stable owner scope; requestId and workspace epoch change do not enter queuedIntentCommitment bytes. That MAC covers only fixed domain, stable scope and canonical bytes. With the old bare-key deletion, the same cached HMAC key signs identical bytes and commitments remain equal, failing the new inequality. With exact cache deletion, volatile key is newly generated and commitment differs. AES-GCM random IV cannot make this comparison pass because payloadCommitment is the deterministic HMAC, not ciphertext hash.

Old grant becomes invalid before retireWorkspace and its local seal returns stale-owner. Separate workspace commitment is unchanged after original workspace retirement, detecting a broad intentMacKeys.clear workaround. Ciphertext/plaintext test buffers are wiped and provider disposed. Existing persistent reload tests remain unchanged; the correction preserves intentional durable key reload.

Only helper naming and exact cache deletion changed in production. workspaceGrantValid, localRequestCurrent, owner/generation rechecks around awaits, nonextractable key generation, purpose/target AAD and durable IDB key names/rows are preserved. No new crypto primitive, wire/envelope version, public getter, storage schema or namespace migration introduced.
